Paste detection was built for a quieter problem
“I need live proctoring. How do I know if a candidate is using an invisible AI overlay?”
That’s a real review of our own platform, left in 2025. It’s now the most common question buyers bring us.
The gap is evidence. When a score is questioned, your team needs to see how the work was produced.
Paste detection
catches a paste. It does not catch a candidate retyping an AI answer line by line from a second screen. Codility offers pattern detection exactly for this problem.
Screen sharing
shows you the screen. Tools like Cluely and Interview Coder are excluded from screen capture, so the screen looks clean.
Session recording
gives you footage that is difficult to watch at scale. An hour of video per candidate does not scale past a handful of roles.
Exam proctoring platforms
were built to monitor a room for universities and certification bodies. They cannot tell you how a piece of code came to exist.
Integrity signals, assembled into something a person can review
Integrity is built into Screen, Interview and Skills Intelligence. Behavioral events, code history, similarity matches, identity checks and network checks feed a single risk level on every candidate report: none, low, moderate or high. Plus pattern detection and invisible AI overlay detection.
Your reviewer opens the level, sees which categories contributed, and drills into the evidence underneath. Codility shows its work. Your reviewer makes the call.

One risk level instead of a wall of flags
Integrity Risk gives you one risk level across behavioral events, cross-candidate similarity, identity verification status and network checks: none, low, moderate or high. A confirmed similarity match raises it automatically.
Deterministic rules produce it, so the same inputs always give the same result.
Your team reviews the sessions that warrant it rather than all of them
Catch the tools that hide from screen sharing
AI overlay apps show candidates answers in a window that screen sharing never picks up. The Codility App, a lightweight desktop app for macOS and Windows, catches those tools on the candidate’s device during the assessment and flags them on the candidate report.
Candidates take the assessment inside the Codility App, so the check runs on their device, not just in the browser.
So the check still works on tools sold as “undetectable.”
It checks the device only. It doesn’t record the screen or log keystrokes.
You turn it on per assessment, so candidates only install it where the stakes justify it.

Every signal is evidence, and a reviewer weighs it before anything happens to the candidate.
Two things a reviewer can check for themselves
1. The risk level is deterministic
Fixed rules, no generative model, and the same inputs always produce the same result. Your reviewer can walk an auditor through every step of how a level was reached. A machine-learned score can’t be walked through that way.
2. The device check targets the evasion technique itself
Most platforms monitor for known keyboard shortcuts, and newer overlay tools have already adapted to that. The Codility App uses a different method to detect how these tools try to game the system.
Built to survive a legal review
No AI or machine learning makes automated employment decisions. Scoring is deterministic and a human is accountable for every outcome.
Codility does not train AI models on your candidate or employee data. That holds across every account, and no setting changes it.

Questions buyers ask
Not reliably. Published research on AI-code detection tools finds critical precision and recall trade-offs and concludes that reliable detection does not currently exist. Codility gives your reviewer the evidence of how the code was produced: typing patterns, the code evolution timeline, paste and focus events, and a device check for programs hiding from screen capture.
These tools stay invisible to screen sharing by asking the operating system to exclude them from screen capture. Browser-based proctoring can’t see that, because the tool runs outside the browser. Codility’s cheating apps detection has the candidate work inside the Codility App, a desktop app for macOS and Windows that looks for programs requesting screen-capture exclusion.
An AI proctored remote team assessment is one a candidate takes from their own location while the platform records integrity signals automatically: behavioral events such as pastes and focus changes, identity verification, network checks, similarity against other submissions, and optionally webcam or screen recording. In hiring, those signals give a reviewer something to inspect before they decide.
Only where video and screen proctoring is switched on for that assessment, and candidates are told before they begin. The Codility App used for device checks is separate: it looks for known cheating tools on the device without recording the screen or logging keystrokes.
No. Codility does not auto-fail anybody on an integrity signal. The risk level is decision support. Reviewers see which categories contributed and open the evidence underneath before they act on it.
Ask whether individual flags resolve into one reviewable risk level or stay a scatter of binary alerts. A deterministic risk level can be walked through step by step for an auditor and a machine-learned one cannot, so ask which you are buying. Then ask what the device check looks at: how overlay tools evade screen capture, or a list of known keyboard shortcuts. Codility folds behavioral, similarity, identity and network signals into one risk level with four steps. Fixed rules produce it, and the device check looks at screen-capture evasion.
Most Codility signals are passive and run after submission, so candidates take a normal assessment. Across 48,000+ post-assessment responses, 91% say the content is fair and 87% rate the experience good or excellent. Webcam recording and ID verification are opt-in premium features with clear candidate consent.
Codility does not use AI or machine learning to make automated employment decisions, and applies deterministic, transparent scoring. Local Law 144 is written around exactly that. Integrity Risk runs on fixed rules, so you can reconstruct every rating step by step for a high-risk employment review under the EU AI Act. SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR and CCPA apply throughout, with EU or US data residency chosen at contract time.
Aggregating across categories is what reduces that. A single paste event does not produce a high risk level on its own. Reviewers see which categories contributed and can drill into the evidence before acting.
Live interviews cover a fraction of most pipelines. Screen assessments carry the volume and need integrity coverage too. In Interview, behavioral signals surface to the interviewer during the session, so they can probe a focus change or a large insertion while the candidate is still in the room.
